results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 67 prose units' outline summaries match the controlling ideas of their aligned spec paragraphs, in spec order (p01-p67, with prediction p37-p39 before migrations p32-p36 as the spec orders sections); the five callouts are front matter outside the paragraph alignment.

The outliner marked Introduction ¶3 as two ideas (category as first governed reference + roadmap). The opening sentences are the setup for one controlling idea the spec itself declares for p03: this chapter designs the tree behind the category ID, section by section. The first half motivates the roadmap rather than arguing a separate point.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim: intro and scene to C1; controls to C1; structure to C2; versioned to C3; external to C4; prediction and migrations to C5; practice to C5/C6; trade-offs, verticals and failures to C1-C5; Chief Architect's view to C6; questions and conclusion to the thesis and so-what.

Each table (dependencies, structures, country models, release artifacts, service interfaces, external taxonomies, operations, tiers, other concerns, trade-offs, verticals, change classes, metrics), Figures 1-6 and each quotation (eBay leaf rule and categoryTreeVersion, Amazon 'place(s)', Google vehicle changelog and redirects, Auto Trader, eBay 'magical listing', Mercari 'performed satisfactorily') is introduced and its bearing on the claim stated in the adjacent prose or caption.
All declared transition_in relationships are expressed at their boundaries (several via the subheading plus the opening phrase) except the one failed below at In Practice ¶5.

results.draft_locus: In Practice: The Bikes Split at Veldmark ¶5
results.quote: Femke's Rotterdam city bike, sold in March 2027 and archived, illustrates the version rule from [[listing-aggregate]]
results.finding: The spec declares a contrast at the start of p44 (live listings that moved vs an archived listing that did not). The opening sentence instead introduces a new example of the listing-aggregate version rule with no contrast to the 410,000 moved listings; the contrast is only implicit in 'still says' mid-sentence. Flow reader B independently found the paragraph 'sits oddly' at this boundary.

results.quote: A model trained on version 2027.10 cannot predict leaves that exist only in 2027.11.
results.finding: Veldmark's release numbers are used as if known two sections before In Practice establishes 2027.10 as the canonical tree's first release and 2027.11 as the bikes release; both flow readers stopped here (A: a forward reference; B: wondered whether they had missed where the numbers were introduced). The spec's order is fine; a generic label or a clause naming the releases fixes it.
results.corroborated_by: Flow reader B, section 3 'Terms used before they are explained', second bullet (same sentence quoted); reader A item 9 is the first report.

results.quote: The 230,000 listings in sport-bike and parts leaves mapped one to one.
results.finding: The one-to-one leaves are called 'sport-bike and parts leaves' here and in the scene, but 'road, mountain, and parts and accessories' in Figure 5 and In Practice ¶2; both flow readers had to stop and match the names. Use one name set.
results.corroborated_by: Flow reader B, section 3 'Small consistency snags', first bullet (same mismatch); reader A item 7 is the first report.

Names the flow readers found unexplained (Yardstick, Common Ground, Motorvane, Hearthly, Femke, Essen Golf, 'share platforms, not products') belong to the book's cast, brands and earlier chapters, which audience.already_knows covers.
Opens with a thought-provoking question and two contrasting answers, then the bridge and roadmap; no dictionary, history or announcement opening.
The conclusion synthesizes and states a measure and hand-off; it neither merely restates nor introduces a new argument.
'Daan's six weeks were never a cost of the tree... move the cost of a change from the tree to the migration: Fatbikes took two days. Lead time for a new category is the measure to watch.'
Calls back to 'where the listing goes' (now the navigation layer only) and Daan's six weeks from the opening.

The intro-only reader predicted the sections in order (six-week problem, what a category controls, structure, versioned releases, external mappings, prediction, migrations, bikes split and harmonization, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, governance, hand-off) and the evidence (eBay, Amazon, Google, Shopify, Mercari, fictional Veldmark). Its Tradeyard/Veldmark query is answered for this audience, which knows Veldmark's brands.

Reader listed the release contents (new tree with stable IDs, mapping for every retired node, attribute diff, effective dates) and the rest: rules/model-above-threshold/seller reclassification gated by an audit, saved searches rewritten to preserve results, 301s, partner codes accepted for a window with warnings, search mappings and models updated, analytics mapping view, country views keeping local labels and navigation.

Reader named the Category Straitjacket (category treated as content while behaving as a schema key; IDs, names and slugs hard-coded; divergent country trees) and the fix: one canonical tree with stable meaningless IDs, rules reading properties from the taxonomy service, navigation/labels/slugs separate, versioned releases consumers pin, and lead time as the metric.

Reader explained one destination per listing in a merge vs a per-listing decision and a default-only mapping in a split, described Mercari's LLM labeling of several million items among generated candidates with kNN propagation over embeddings including the original category, and stated Mercari published no accuracy figure.
Reader chose an attribute (electric assist on Cargo bikes; cargo wins over electric) by the changes-a-contract rule and classed it as additive, taxonomy team review, two days.
